newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indexes slow as bounce continues.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indexes slow as bounce continues.

text.p: Trading in major U.S. stock index options cooled Tuesday as the market continued to recover from last Friday's steep selloff.
"All the premiums are still so high in the indexes," one options dealer in Chicago said. "I don't see a lot of buying or selling."

High premiums aside, volatilities continued to ease as the market worked its way higher. The volatility index, which is priced off certain front-month S&P 100 index options, was down a point, or about 3.8 percent, at 25.14, in early afternoon action.
The options dealer said the market was probably being helped along by short-covering but that it appeared some investors were not concerned about a retest of last week's lows.
"There's no panic in the street," he said. "They weathered the big drop and people are loading up again."
By about 1220 CDT/1720 GMT, the Dow industrial average, which fell 336 points last week, was ahead roughly 63 points at 7,866. It rallied 109 points Monday.
The OEX gained nearly eight to 895.67 and the broader S&P 500 index .SPX rose about nine to 921.43. September S&P 500 futures rose 5.95 to 924.70.
The options dealer said the Dow would likely get stuck around the 8,000 level and trade around there until after the U.S. Labor Day holiday on September 1.
"Probably once we get to 8,000 we'll see some selling," he said.
Chris Cadbury, who publishes a daily market letter, said he doubted the market had much upside potential left.

Cadbury said some of the market's gains Monday and Tuesday were from shorts covering positions ahead of an expected announcement from the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting unit that it would leave interest rates unchanged.
"I think this market has done so well after there have been announcements of no interest rate change in the past that the buying came in perhaps in anticipation," he added.
The Federal Open Market Committee is meeting today on interest rate policy. No change is expected.
Among OEX options, calls began to draw more interest as the market extended its gains.
Trading in OEX options was led by the September 900 calls, which traded nearly 3,100 contracts. The September 910 calls traded 2,530 and the September 940 calls traded 2,225.
The OEX September 830 puts were the most active with turnover of roughly 2,100 contracts.

In the SPX, however, puts continued to trade actively as about 6,265 September 910 puts changed hands. The September 850 puts traded 4,360 contracts. The most active call was the September 930 with turnover of 1,415 contracts.
